programs.Country or Region: India (global program; India is eligible where Google Cloud is available for self-service purchasing)
programs.Benefit Summary: Up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits over two years for funded startups; includes credits for Gemini/Gemma frontier models, 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus, monthly Google Maps Platform credits, and technical/product support. Google also lists a $2,000 Start tier for qualifying very early startups.
programs.Program Status: Active; applications available
programs.Eligibility: Pre-Seed to Series A startups generally founded within the last 3-5 years, with an active business website and matching business email/domain and Google Cloud billing account. Google says customers must be located where Google Cloud is generally available and self-service purchasing is available. The Scale tiers require verifiable venture funding; government grants, loans, crowdfunding, and friends-and-family funding do not qualify for Scale, though other tiers may be considered.
programs.Research Notes: India eligibility is based on provider availability criteria, not Google headquarters location. The official page does not publish a promo/referral code; application is direct.

programs.Country or Region: India (global program; India startups can apply subject to AWS Activate eligibility)
programs.Benefit Summary: AWS states eligible startups can receive up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits for infrastructure, data services, and AI/ML models, including third-party models on Amazon Bedrock.
programs.Program Status: Active; applications available
programs.Eligibility: Startups at stages from first prototype through Series A and beyond may apply, subject to AWS Activate terms and approval. Provider eligibility review applies; the page does not state an India exclusion.
programs.Research Notes: AWS headquarters/provider origin is not the region criterion; India startups are covered through the global application subject to terms. No provider-published code appears on the official page.

programs.Country or Region: India (global program; India founders can apply through the startup portal)
programs.Benefit Summary: Access to AI models and developer tools plus up to $150,000 in credits, usable across eligible Azure services. The program also advertises free access to tools and Microsoft customer-network/go-to-market support.
programs.Program Status: Active; enrollment available
programs.Eligibility: Startups/founders building and scaling technology products can enroll through Microsoft for Startups. The official page describes startup credits, AI services, technical resources, and go-to-market support; final acceptance and benefit allocation occur through the Microsoft for Startups portal.
programs.Research Notes: The public landing page is US-localized but describes a global startup offering; India eligibility should be confirmed during portal enrollment. No public promo/referral code is listed.

programs.Benefit Summary: Up to ₹20 lakh grant for proof-of-concept, prototype development, or product trials, plus up to ₹50 lakh investment for market entry, commercialization, or scaling through convertible debentures, debt, or debt-linked instruments. A startup may receive each instrument once under the scheme.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to ₹70 lakh combined (₹20 lakh grant + ₹50 lakh investment), subject to separate eligibility and selection
programs.Program Status: Active scheme; online application process/portal available, with calls opened on the Startup India portal
programs.Eligibility: DPIIT-recognized startup incorporated no more than two years before application; only eligible incorporated entities (private limited company, registered partnership, or LLP) can apply, not individual entrepreneurs. Sector-agnostic, with preference for specified innovation/social-impact sectors. Applications are online through eligible incubators.
programs.Research Notes: Official FAQ gives the exact grant and investment ceilings and says no application fee. This is a Government of India program; no promo/referral code is applicable or published.

programs.Benefit Summary: Guarantee cover for debt facilities to DPIIT-recognized startups, with maximum debt eligible for guarantee cover revised to ₹20 crore per borrower. Transaction-based cover is 85% of amount in default for loans up to ₹10 crore and 75% for loans above ₹10 crore, subject to scheme rules; the guarantee is issued through eligible member institutions, not directly to startups.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to ₹20 crore debt eligible for guarantee cover per borrower
programs.Program Status: Active; applications routed through Jan Samarth or member lending institutions
programs.Eligibility: DPIIT-recognized startup, not in default or classified as NPA, and certified eligible by a member institution. Eligible lenders include scheduled commercial banks, qualifying RBI-registered NBFCs, and SEBI-registered AIFs/venture debt funds. Startup approaches the lender; NCGTC provides cover to the lender.
programs.Research Notes: The official Startup India page was last updated 14-SEP-2026 and lists Jan Samarth plus member institutions as application routes. This is a guarantee, not a cash grant or direct credit line; no code applies.

programs.Benefit Type: Equity-free accelerator, product credits, AI access, and cloud/TPU benefits
programs.Benefit Summary: Equity-free accelerator support including dedicated Google/industry experts, mentoring, technical deep dives, early access to AI products, Google product credits, and free Cloud TPU access for eligible open-source ML research. Cloud credits may be applied for separately and require eligibility review; the page does not state a fixed rupee/dollar amount for accelerator product credits.
programs.Program Status: Closed for the 2026 cohort; official page lists applications closed 19-Apr-2026, kickoff June 2026, graduation September 2026
programs.Eligibility: Startups based/headquartered in India, ideally Seed to Series A, with traction, scalable and defensible products, and deeply technical AI/ML focus. The 2026 cohort targeted core AI products/foundation models and required founder/team participation.
programs.Research Notes: The page explicitly distinguishes India headquarters eligibility and says the accelerator is equity-free. Product-credit amount is not published; Cloud credits link to the separate Google Cloud program. No public code is listed.

programs.Country or Region: India (available globally subject to approved partner/funding verification)
programs.Benefit Summary: Eligible funded startups receive 90% off in year one, 50% off in year two, and 25% off in year three for net-new Professional or Enterprise products. Startups associated with an approved entrepreneurial organization receive 30% off in year one and 15% off in year two.
programs.Program Status: Active; applications available
programs.Eligibility: For the 90% tier: pre-seed, seed, or Series A funding (not Series B+) and affiliation with an approved HubSpot for Startups partner or verified venture funding. For the 30% tier: association with an approved entrepreneurial organization. Applies to net-new Professional/Enterprise products; India startups can qualify through partner or funding verification.
programs.Research Notes: Discount is applied through eligibility verification and signup, not a public coupon. HubSpot’s official page does not publish a promo/referral code.

programs.Benefit Summary: Eligible bootstrapped startups incorporated in India receive 30% off HubSpot paid tools in the first year, plus startup resources, training, support, and networking.
programs.Program Status: Active; applications available
programs.Eligibility: Company must be incorporated in India (listed explicitly), founded within the last five years, meet regional employee-count and revenue limits, have 1-25 employees depending on region, not be an agency or affiliated with a VC/accelerator/incubator, and be a technology company serving B2B/B2C markets. Program membership is free; discount applies to net-new paid products.
programs.Research Notes: India is expressly listed among eligible Asian incorporation countries. The official page says the application is reviewed by HubSpot; no public code is provided.

programs.Benefit Summary: Four-week early-stage SaaS accelerator with tailored mentorship, technical deep dives, community, enterprise exposure, and potential AWS Activate credits of up to $25,000 for cohort participants.
programs.Program Status: Closed; official page shows the last published application window as 13-Aug-2024 to 10-Sep-2024 and program sessions in September-October 2024
programs.Eligibility: Early-stage funded or unfunded startups headquartered in India and other APJ countries, seeking product-market fit; startups must also qualify for AWS Activate credit program.
programs.Research Notes: Included because it is explicitly India-eligible and materially startup-specific, but applicants should wait for a new cohort announcement; the official page does not show an active application window or public code.

programs.Benefit Summary: Ukraine-based startups selected through the fund received equity-free cash awards of up to $100,000, ongoing Google mentorship and product support, and up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits. Google’s June 2025 announcement identifies that cohort as the final cohort.
programs.Maximum Value: $100,000 non-dilutive funding plus $350,000 Google Cloud credits
programs.Program Status: Closed to new applications; final cohort announced June 11, 2025
programs.Eligibility: Ukraine-based startups selected through the fund; the official page describes support for Ukrainian entrepreneurs and the final cohort was operated with Ukrainian accelerator 1991.
programs.Research Notes: Provider headquarters is not the eligibility basis: this was explicitly a Ukraine-based startup fund. Google’s official announcement says the June 2025 cohort was final, so treat this as historical/alumni support rather than an open application.

programs.Provider: Microsoft for Startups / Ukrainian Startup Fund
programs.Program Name: Microsoft Azure credits for USF-collaborating Ukrainian startups
programs.Benefit Summary: Startups that have collaborated with the Ukrainian Startup Fund can apply for Microsoft Azure credits/loans worth up to $150,000 equivalent for cloud infrastructure, storage, AI/ML, product development and scaling.
programs.Program Status: Active/currently described by Ukraine’s Ministry of Digital Transformation page (published February 25, 2026); application form linked
programs.Eligibility: Pre-seed through Series A; software-based core product; owns its software; less than $350,000 in Azure credits received over time; registered where Azure is available; not Series C or later; privately held and for-profit; not consulting, educational, government or crypto-mining. Must have collaborated with USF.
programs.Research Notes: The Ukraine government page says USF joined Microsoft for Startups Investor Network and gives the Ukraine-specific route. Microsoft’s provider page independently advertises up to $150,000 in startup credits, but the USF collaboration requirement is the Ukraine-specific condition.

programs.Benefit Summary: USF’s announced Startup EDGE grant program supports Ukrainian Deep Tech, Green Tech and EdTech startups with pre-seed grants up to €20,000 and seed grants up to €40,000.
programs.Program Status: Upcoming/pre-registration; official page says “Call for Applications coming soon”
programs.Eligibility: Ukrainian early-stage startups in Deep Tech, Green Tech or EdTech. The page lists sectors including AI/ML, biotech/life sciences, MedTech, robotics, advanced materials, quantum, IoT, cybersecurity, SpaceTech, electronics, photonics, 5G, Web3, renewables, clean technology and digital learning.
programs.Research Notes: This is a Ukraine-focused USF program supported by the EU-funded, French-co-funded EU4Innovation East project. The page offers an email pre-registration list, not an open grant application yet.

programs.Provider: Ukrainian Startup Fund / Western NIS Enterprise Fund
programs.Program Name: Grant Programme to support Ukrainian technology companies
programs.Benefit Summary: The program offered up to $25,000 for pre-seed projects and up to $50,000 for seed projects, with a total program budget of $2.5 million and planned support for 74 teams.
programs.Program Status: Expired/closed based on stated program duration ending December 31, 2025
programs.Eligibility: Profit or social-effect business entities legally registered; total prior investments/grants/state support no more than $500,000; annual income no more than $500,000; not operating in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories or under sanctions. Military-product projects and projects funded by BRAVE1 or Seeds of Bravery were excluded.
programs.Research Notes: The official announcement says applications were submitted on a regular basis but explicitly states program duration until December 31, 2025; do not assume the portal still accepts this specific call after that date.

programs.Provider: Seeds of Bravery (UASEEDs) / European Union EIC
programs.Program Name: Seeds of Bravery Ukrainian tech startup support
programs.Benefit Summary: EU-funded project for Ukrainian tech startups offering non-refundable grants up to €60,000 total across five support programs, plus market discovery, fast-track programs, deep-tech incubation/acceleration, investor matchmaking and EIC application support.
programs.Program Status: Completed/closed; official site says the last cohort was awarded and describes the project in past tense
programs.Eligibility: Ukrainian tech startups; program tracks covered Business and Innovation Services, Innovative Entrepreneurship, Deep Tech Incubators, Rebuild Ukraine, and Deep Tech Scale-up and Acceleration.
programs.Research Notes: The official site says it was a €20 million EU project and that €12 million was allocated in non-refundable grants. Its news section states the last cohort had been awarded, so this is a completed opportunity, not an open call.

programs.Country or Region: Ukraine (conditional on Google Cloud regional availability and self-service purchasing)
programs.Benefit Summary: Eligible funded startups can receive up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits over two years, credits for frontier models such as Gemini and Gemma, 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus at no extra cost, and monthly Google Maps Platform credits.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to $350,000 Google Cloud credits over two years, plus 12 months Workspace Business Plus and monthly Maps credits
programs.Program Status: Active application program
programs.Eligibility: Pre-seed to Series A startups generally founded within the last 3–5 years, with verifiable funding for funded tiers; applicants need an active business website, matching business email/domain and Google Cloud billing account. Google says customers must be in a region where Google Cloud is generally available and self-service purchasing is available. Ukraine-specific acceptance is not separately enumerated on the page and remains subject to Google review.
programs.Research Notes: This is not Ukraine-exclusive; Ukraine eligibility is based on the provider’s regional availability rule, not Google’s headquarters. Credits generally apply to Google Cloud products; Workspace, Maps and other Google products are separate offers. The $350,000 figure is the current official maximum for funded/AI tiers, while the FAQ also describes a $200,000 Scale tier.

programs.Country or Region: Ukraine (global program; country-specific acceptance not enumerated)
programs.Benefit Summary: AWS says eligible startups can apply for up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits for infrastructure, data services and AI/ML models, including third-party models on Amazon Bedrock.
programs.Program Status: Active application program
programs.Eligibility: Startups at stages from prototype through Series A and beyond may use AWS for Startups resources; credit approval is subject to AWS Activate eligibility and application review. The official page does not publish a Ukraine-specific exclusion or a country list, so Ukrainian startups should confirm account and regional eligibility in the application flow.
programs.Research Notes: Provider headquarters is not the eligibility basis. AWS presents Activate as a global startup program and does not show a Ukraine-specific promo/referral code on the official page; credits are application-based rather than redeemed with a public code.

programs.Program Name: Israel Startups Digital Hub / Google Cloud Startup Program
programs.Benefit Type: Cloud credits; technical and go-to-market support
programs.Benefit Summary: Google’s Israel-specific startup hub advertises up to $350,000 in Google Cloud credits, local/Hebrew expert access, generative-AI training, startup events, and Google Cloud Marketplace/go-to-market support.
programs.Program Status: Open; official page says Apply now
programs.Eligibility: Startups in Israel; detailed tier eligibility is handled through the Google Cloud startup application and review. The hub explicitly targets startups in Israel.
programs.Research Notes: Israel eligibility is explicit. The page does not publish a promo/referral code; credits are application-based.

programs.Benefit Summary: For eligible VC-funded AI startups using or planning to use Gemini as a core product technology: up to $250,000 in year-one credits for AI-first startups plus up to $100,000 in year-two credits, for a stated maximum of $350,000 over two years. Includes AI expert access and credits for Gemini/Gemma.
programs.Program Status: Open; Apply now is published
programs.Eligibility: VC-funded startups founded within five years; Pre-Seed/Seed funding within the last five years or Series A within the last 12 months; Gemini is or will be foundational to the primary product; not previously received more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits. Google says acceptance is discretionary. Israel is not excluded; this is a global Google Cloud program.
programs.Research Notes: Provider is global/US-headquartered; eligibility here is based on the global application being available and no Israel exclusion, not on Google’s headquarters location.

programs.Program Name: Google for Startups Accelerator: Europe and Israel (Energy 2026)
programs.Benefit Type: Equity-free accelerator; product credits; AI access; TPU access; mentoring
programs.Benefit Summary: Three-month hybrid/equity-free accelerator with Google expert mentoring, technical workshops, early access to AI products, eligible Google product credits, and free Cloud TPU access. Cloud credits require a separate application and eligibility review.
programs.Program Status: Applications closed; interest registration open for future programs
programs.Eligibility: Tech startups with HQ in Europe and Israel, typically Pre-Seed to Post-Series A, traction, scalable/deeply technical AI/ML products, and solutions for grid modernization, demand flexibility, or energy affordability/cost savings. Official page lists June 12, 2026 application close.
programs.Research Notes: Israel eligibility is explicit in the program name and HQ criteria. No fixed credit amount or public code is stated; cloud credits are subject to separate review.

programs.Benefit Type: Cloud, infrastructure, data, and AI/ML credits
programs.Benefit Summary: AWS states that startups can apply for up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits, usable against infrastructure, data services, and AI/ML models, including third-party models on Amazon Bedrock.
programs.Program Status: Open; Apply now published
programs.Eligibility: Startups at any stage may apply subject to AWS Activate eligibility and review; the official page does not exclude Israel. Higher credit levels generally depend on startup stage or an Activate provider relationship.
programs.Research Notes: AWS is US-headquartered; this record concerns Israel-based startup eligibility for the global program, not AWS headquarters. No public promo/referral code appears on the official page.

programs.Benefit Type: Azure cloud credits; AI and developer tools; go-to-market support
programs.Benefit Summary: Microsoft advertises up to $150,000 in credits, access to AI models and developer tools, technical resources, and Microsoft customer-network/go-to-market support.
programs.Program Status: Open; Claim benefits/Get started links active
programs.Eligibility: Startups applying through Microsoft for Startups; specific qualification and benefit level are determined in the startup portal. The global program page does not exclude Israel.
programs.Research Notes: Microsoft is US-headquartered; Israel is treated as a potential eligible location under the global application, subject to portal review. The official page publishes no referral code.

programs.Benefit Type: Non-dilutive public investment/grant matched with private capital
programs.Benefit Summary: For Israeli deep-tech/R&D-intensive startups: Pre-Seed grant covers 60% of the round up to NIS 2 million; Seed covers 50% up to NIS 6 million; Round A covers 30% up to NIS 15 million. Preferred companies can receive an additional 10%, with listed maxima of NIS 2.2m, NIS 6.6m, and NIS 16.5m where applicable.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to 15,000,000 (standard Round A maximum); up to 16,500,000 for qualifying preferred Round A companies
programs.Program Status: Open yearlong
programs.Eligibility: Legally incorporated Israeli companies at Pre-Seed, Seed, or Round A, primarily conducting industrial R&D in Israel, within the stated funding, income, round-size, and private-investor matching thresholds. Authority takes no equity or voting rights.
programs.Research Notes: This is explicitly Israel-specific. It is a grant/non-dilutive investment requiring matching private funding, not a coupon or provider credit.

programs.Program Name: Fast-Track Program for Startups and Early-Stage Growth Companies Affected by Shekel Appreciation
programs.Benefit Summary: NIS 1 billion program intended to extend runway by six months. Grants cover 33% or 50% of required funding, approximately two or three months of runway, with matching financing required; maximum grant is NIS 15 million.
programs.Program Status: Launched; applications opened July 29, 2026; no closing date stated on official announcement
programs.Eligibility: Israeli technology startups/early-stage growth companies no more than 15 years old, with less than 12 months runway, annual expenses of NIS 1.5m–100m, at least 50% of expenses on R&D and at least 50% incurred in Israel and denominated in NIS; additional revenue/fx conditions apply for revenue-financed companies.
programs.Research Notes: Official announcement gives exact maximum and eligibility but does not display a promo/referral code.

programs.Provider: Directorate of Defense Research & Development (DDR&D), Israel Ministry of Defense
programs.Benefit Type: Non-equity grant; defense-tech accelerator; validation and mentoring
programs.Benefit Summary: Selected dual-use technology ventures receive an initial NIS 200,000 grant without equity or IP dilution, plus a six-month acceleration program, Ministry of Defense/IDF technical validation, SOSA or iHLS business support, and investor/industry exposure.
programs.Program Status: Registration closed
programs.Eligibility: Israeli/eligible startups matching published defense and dual-use challenges; each cycle selects approximately 12–16 companies. Official page says hundreds apply and lists cloud/security, AI, sensing, robotics, energy, and other challenge areas.
programs.Research Notes: Israel-specific government/defense program. The official page explicitly shows Registration Closed; monitor the DDR&D page for the next cycle.

programs.Benefit Type: Cloud credits; discounts; technical and support benefits
programs.Benefit Summary: Three-year startup program with up to $120,000 in first-year cloud credits, plus discounted cloud services in years two and three, dedicated account management, solutions-engineering guidance, and priority 24/7/365 support.
programs.Program Status: Open; application form active
programs.Eligibility: Early-stage, for-profit companies under seven years old with at least one qualifying traction/funding/revenue indicator, a plan to scale on Akamai Cloud, a new Akamai account, corporate website/email, and valid card. The application country selector includes Israel.
programs.Research Notes: Israel eligibility is evidenced by Israel being available in the official application country selector. Provider is global/US-headquartered; no public code is shown.

programs.Benefit Type: Developer platform, infrastructure, security, and AI credits
programs.Benefit Summary: Tiered one-year program: $10,000 for bootstrapped/self-funded startups under $1m raised; $100,000 for startups under $5m raised and funded by an affiliated partner; or $350,000 for startups with $5m+ raised and an affiliated partner. Includes usage credits, security/networking features, and tier-dependent support.
programs.Program Status: Open; official page says Apply now
programs.Eligibility: For-profit technology product companies founded within 10 years, funded up to Series B within the last 12 months, with a public website and public social profile; first-time applicants only. Israel is not excluded by the global application.
programs.Research Notes: Global provider program, not Israel-specific; Israel-based applicants must satisfy the published criteria. Credits expire after one year or when consumed. No public promo/referral code is published.

programs.Benefit Type: Cloud credits; AI/GPU opportunities; SaaS partner perks
programs.Benefit Summary: Selected startups receive 12 months of DigitalOcean credits (amount varies by award/partner), expert one-on-ones, 15 months of Standard-tier paid support, and partner perks including Airtable $2,000 credit, Notion $1,000 credit, QuickNode up to $5,000, 100ms $2,500, HubSpot up to 90% off year one, and other listed benefits.
programs.Maximum Value: Unknown for core credits; partner perks include up to 5,000 (QuickNode) and listed fixed amounts
programs.Program Status: Open; official application link active
programs.Eligibility: Prioritizes AI-native startups; must have raised $10m or less, have a company website and matching company email, and create a registered DigitalOcean team account. Applicants need not be VC-backed and can select Other for partner organization. Service businesses/agencies are excluded. Israel is not excluded.
programs.Research Notes: The current official page says the core credit amount varies and that GPU credits are separately reviewed; do not treat the listed partner perks as guaranteed cash-equivalent credits. Provider is US-headquartered; Israel eligibility is via the global application.

programs.Benefit Type: Database credits; AI model tokens; technical support
programs.Benefit Summary: Stage-based startup program offering Atlas credits and Voyage AI tokens, technical expertise, and dedicated support. Exact credit amount is tier-dependent and not published on the current official page.
programs.Program Status: Open; Apply Now published
programs.Eligibility: Base-tier criteria include early-stage company under seven years old and Series A or earlier, scalable software product/service, no prior acceptance, active website and LinkedIn. Applications can be direct or through a VC/accelerator/incubator; Israel is not excluded.
programs.Research Notes: The official FAQ says accepted startups receive a unique promo code in the welcome email, but no provider-published public code is available; therefore the code field is blank. Provider is US-headquartered; this is global program eligibility.

programs.Benefit Summary: Ten-week hybrid, equity-free accelerator for Brazilian Seed to Series A startups, with Google mentoring, technical projects, early access to AI products, product credits, possible Google Cloud credits subject to separate eligibility review, and free Cloud TPU access.
programs.Program Status: Applications closed; page invites interest registration for future programs. The 2026 cohort dates shown are applications Jan 12-Mar 1, kickoff May, graduation/demo day July.
programs.Eligibility: Seed to Series A, headquartered in Brazil, ideally revenue-generating and using ML/AI; scalable technical product; minimum five employees in addition to founder; CTO/technical leads must participate.
programs.Research Notes: Region eligibility is explicit (headquartered in Brazil). Google, not Brazil, is the provider headquarters. The page says eligible startups receive product credits but gives no amount.

programs.Benefit Type: Cloud credits; SaaS discount; AI/API credits
programs.Benefit Summary: Cloud credits for startup infrastructure, frontier models including Gemini/Gemma, technical training, 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus at no extra cost, and monthly Google Maps Platform credits as separate benefits.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to $350,000 over two years; Start tier $2,000; funded tiers $200,000-$350,000
programs.Program Status: Open application
programs.Eligibility: Pre-Seed to Series A startups founded within roughly 3-5 years; funded tiers require verifiable qualifying equity funding. Customer must be in a region where Google Cloud is generally available and self-service purchasing is available; Brazil is not excluded. Program acceptance is discretionary.
programs.Research Notes: Global program; provider headquarters is not the eligibility criterion. Credits generally cannot be applied to subscription-billed products or third-party Marketplace products; Workspace and Maps benefits are separate.

programs.Program Name: Google for Startups Cloud AI Program
programs.Benefit Summary: AI-focused Scale tier with Google Cloud credits covering Google models such as Gemini and Gemma, plus AI expert webinars, Q&As, technical support and enablement.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to $350,000 over two years (up to $250,000 in year 1 for AI-first startups plus up to $100,000 in year 2)
programs.Program Status: Open application
programs.Eligibility: VC-funded startups using or planning to use Gemini as a foundation of their primary product; Pre-Seed/Seed raised within five years or Series A within 12 months; founded within five years; not previously received more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits. Acceptance discretionary.
programs.Research Notes: Brazil is eligible insofar as Google Cloud is available there and the startup meets the global criteria; the page does not list a Brazil-specific restriction. Third-party models are not covered by these credits.

programs.Benefit Summary: Promotional AWS credits usable for infrastructure, data services and AI/ML, including eligible third-party models on Amazon Bedrock. Self-funded founders can start at $1,000 and may receive up to $5,000; provider-backed startups can receive up to $200,000; additional AI credits are invite-only.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to $200,000; $200,000+ additional AI credits by invitation
programs.Program Status: Open application
programs.Eligibility: Pre-Series B, founded within the last 10 years, AWS account on paid tier, and either new to Activate credits or seeking more than previously received. Portfolio tier requires an Activate Provider Organization ID; Founders tier is available to bootstrapped/self-funded startups.
programs.Research Notes: Global AWS program; Brazil is not excluded and applications are made through the global portal. Provider/accelerator affiliation is an eligibility route, not a Brazil-specific referral code.

programs.Benefit Type: Cloud credits; AI/API credits; developer SaaS/tools
programs.Benefit Summary: Access to up to $150,000 in credits, Azure AI services/models, developer tools and free access to startup-oriented tools, plus Microsoft customer-network and go-to-market support.
programs.Program Status: Open / join now
programs.Eligibility: Startups/founders joining through the Microsoft for Startups portal; detailed qualification is handled in the portal. Benefits include Azure credits applicable to eligible Azure services and access to AI tools.
programs.Research Notes: Global program page; the URL contains a US locale parameter, but the program is presented as global and does not state that Brazilian startups are excluded. Exact qualification gates are evaluated after joining.

programs.Benefit Summary: Usage credits for Cloudflare developer platform, compute, storage, delivery and Workers AI, plus core security/networking features at no cost, support and technical sessions depending on tier. Credits last one year or until consumed.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to $350,000 for one year; $10,000 Tier 3, $100,000 Tier 2, $350,000 Tier 1
programs.Program Status: Open application
programs.Eligibility: For-profit technology product startup, incorporated within the last 10 years, funded up to Series B within the last 12 months, live public website, public LinkedIn/X/GitHub presence, business-domain email, first-time applicant. Tier 3 requires no minimum funding and under $1M raised; higher tiers require affiliated-partner funding. No Brazil restriction stated.
programs.Research Notes: Global program; Brazil is not excluded. Credits cover usage-based services, with product caps such as Workers AI and R2; AI Gateway is temporarily excluded. Cloudflare is headquartered outside Brazil, which does not determine eligibility.

programs.Benefit Type: Cloud credits; AI infrastructure; SaaS partner perks
programs.Benefit Summary: Twelve months of DigitalOcean credits, expert one-to-ones, Standard-tier paid support for 15 months, startup community and marketplace exposure. The official page also lists partner benefits including Stripe Atlas 20% off, Airtable $2,000 credit, Notion $1,000 credit, Miro $1,000 credit, QuickNode up to $5,000 credit and HubSpot up to 90% off year one.
programs.Maximum Value: Unknown; award varies by approved partner/program review
programs.Program Status: Open application; selected startups may separately be invited to apply for GPU packages
programs.Eligibility: Prioritizes AI-native startups; must have raised $10M or less, have a company website and matching company email, create a registered DigitalOcean team account, and not have used prior DigitalOcean credits. Service-based consultancies/agencies are not eligible. Direct application is available for startups without VC/incubator backing.
programs.Research Notes: Global program; page does not exclude Brazil. The exact credit amount is set in the onboarding email/partner award and therefore is Unknown from the public page. GPU credits are a separate, selective benefit.

programs.Benefit Summary: 90% off year one, 50% off year two and 25% off year three for qualifying funded startups; 30% off year one and 15% off year two for startups associated with an approved entrepreneurial organization. Applies to net-new Professional or Enterprise products.
programs.Maximum Value: Up to 90% discount in year one
programs.Program Status: Open application
